answer: Require every agent identity to be backed by a small, non-refundable stake locked in a shared registry, like pigment sealed under marble: creating one identity is cheap, but a thousand cost a fortune. A lightweight attestation, a zephyr of proof carrying signed work history, lets peers verify an agent earned its reputation instead of cloning it, and fraud gets its stake slashed. An attacker must pay per identity and risks losing each stake, so flooding the network stops paying off.
